intro: A busier Friday: the FTC and 22 states accuse Amazon of secretly jacking up ad prices on Black Friday and Prime Day, TikTok ships a stand-alone Shop app, and affiliate/creator measurement keeps getting a harder look.

must_reads.title: FTC, 22 states accuse Amazon of secretly inflating advertising prices by up to 250%
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: Regulators say Amazon quietly raised the cost of ads around Black Friday and Prime Day by as much as 250%. Peak shopping days are when affiliate links do the most work, so pressure on Amazon’s ad and marketplace rules shapes what sellers and creators can earn.

must_reads.title: TikTok quietly launches a stand-alone TikTok Shop app
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: TikTok is splitting shopping into its own app, which means more of the path from a creator tip to a purchase may stay inside TikTok rather than going out to Amazon or other stores.

must_reads.title: Amazon’s Fees and Ads Near Its Retail Sales
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: Marketplace Pulse says Amazon now takes almost as much from seller fees and ads as it makes from selling goods itself. That squeeze on sellers is the backdrop for every Amazon affiliate and creator programme Geniuslink clients use.

must_reads.title: TikTok Shop Details Livestream Sales Measurement Over 14 Days
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: TikTok Shop now measures livestream sales for 14 days, including buys that finish on a brand’s own site. Platforms that can prove sales beyond the livestream will pull more brand budget into in-app shopping.

must_reads.title: Inside the push for content compensation in the agentic era
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: As AI agents start shopping and summarising content, brands, creators and publishers are arguing about who gets paid. Any new rule for paying the person who pointed a shopper at a product sits next to how affiliate links already work.
